reviews.decision_reason: select_demand applies a demand_score threshold of >=3 and keeps the explicit fallback identifiers in the returned records. In the supplied corpus this retains all eight records, including the fallback records, so it does not localize the observed one-record truncation.

normalize hard-caps the selected demand records to a one-row index window, so the assigned job emits only n06-r01 in both needs and evidence_sources despite the input containing additional allowed demand records. That hides missing and contradictory market-demand evidence instead of preserving the bounded normalized demand set for downstream review.

assemble_provenance ranks whatever normalized records it receives using deterministic demand_score and record_id ordering with missing-safe field access. The one-record provenance output is explained by upstream truncation, not by this boundary.
